name: Slack
verdict: You can have a Slack app installable in any workspace in under 10 minutes, with no review. But if your agent reads channel or thread history, that is throttled to 1 request a minute until Slack approves a Marketplace listing, which takes up to about 12 weeks after you reach 10 active workspaces.

creation.label: Easy
creation.note: About 5 minutes from a manifest. Measured in our test.

approval.label: Hard
approval.note: Marketplace review, gated by 10 active workspaces.

handsOn.note: 10 minutes to a working app. 1 to 2 days to prepare a Marketplace submission.

waiting.note: None to go live. Up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks for Marketplace review.

ownApp.headline: Not to start. Composio has a managed Slack app.
ownApp.note: Move to your own app when you need your brand on the consent screen, scopes beyond Composio's defaults, or your own rate limits instead of a shared quota.

oneWayDoors.title: The workspace that owns the app is permanent.
oneWayDoors.detail: The creation form warns it cannot be changed later, and if you leave that workspace you lose access to the app.
oneWayDoors.doThis: Create the app in a workspace your company owns and will keep, never in a personal or trial workspace.

oneWayDoors.title: Turning distribution off later uninstalls you everywhere.
oneWayDoors.detail: Deactivating public distribution removes the app from every workspace that installed it, and turning it back on means every customer must reinstall.
oneWayDoors.doThis: Treat "Activate Public Distribution" as a one-way door once customers are on it.

oneWayDoors.title: A Marketplace listing locks the app.
oneWayDoors.detail: After approval, any new scope or feature needs a resubmission with a demo video and a staging app, with up to 6 weeks of review.
oneWayDoors.doThis: Request every scope you will need in the next 6 to 12 months before you submit, and keep a separate staging app.

oneWayDoors.title: Token rotation changes how you must store tokens.
oneWayDoors.detail: It is off by default. Once on, tokens expire every 12 hours and each refresh revokes the previous refresh token.
oneWayDoors.doThis: Decide before launch. If you turn it on, store the newest refresh token every time, or connections die with `invalid_grant`.

items.name: Single-workspace
items.when: The default after you create an app.

items.name: Distributed (unlisted)
items.whoCanInstall: Any workspace, through your install link
items.review: None. Took effect instantly in our test.

notes.title: "Stay unlisted forever" is not a real option for a paid product.
notes.text: Slack's API terms say an app that is monetized, or connects to a paid product, needs Slack's authorization to be distributed commercially. For most apps that means the Marketplace; a partner agreement is the alternative. Apps built for one specific customer are exempt.

notes.title: Recommended path for an agent
notes.text: Build single-workspace, activate distribution for beta, and plan the Marketplace from day one if your agent reads messages. Slack's console now also offers an "AI agent" app template and an Agents settings page.

scopes.intro: Agents usually use bot scopes (the app acts as itself, token starts `xoxb-`). User scopes act as the person (`xoxp-`) and are needed for things like search.

rows.impact: 1 req/min, 15 messages per call until listed
1 req/min, 15 messages per call until listed

minimalSets.label: "Summarize my channels" agent
minimalSets.note: Hits the history throttle immediately. See section 8.

changingLater: While unlisted: add scopes freely in the manifest, but every existing workspace must reinstall to grant them. Existing connections do not upgrade on their own.
Once listed: a new scope needs resubmission with a demo video and a staging app.
In Composio: the scopes your auth config requests must match what the app allows, then users reconnect.

toCreate: A company-owned Slack workspace to own the app
A second workspace to test installs as a customer would
An HTTPS redirect URL. For Composio, the callback shown in your auth config
No hard-coded tokens or webhook URLs in your code (you attest to this)
forApproval: 10 or more active workspaces (used in the last 28 days). The counter updates every 24 hours
Public homepage, privacy policy, support contact
Demo video: install, OAuth, setup, real use, uninstall
Test credentials and dummy data for your own product

steps.title: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps
steps.detail: The agent cannot sign in for you. Use the company-owned workspace (decision 1).

steps.title: Create New App, choose "From a manifest"
steps.detail: The dialog also offers AI agent, Starter app and Blank app templates. A manifest is faster and reviewable.

steps.title: Write the manifest
steps.detail: App name, bot user, scopes from section 4, the HTTPS redirect URL, and `token_rotation_enabled` set deliberately.

steps.title: Approve "Create and Install"
steps.detail: Creating and installing into your workspace is now a single step. Settings open at app.slack.com/app-settings.

steps.title: Copy Client ID and Secret into Composio
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config and pass its ID for the slack toolkit. See section 11 on keeping the secret out of sight.

steps.title: Clear the distribution checklist
steps.detail: With a manifest, 3 of 4 items pass automatically. The last is a checkbox confirming no hard-coded tokens.

steps.title: Approve "Activate Public Distribution"
steps.detail: No review. Took effect instantly. Without it, other workspaces get `invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app`.

steps.title: Test install from a second workspace
steps.detail: Use an incognito window, as a new customer would.

stepsNote: Total in our test: about 5 minutes of agent work, one sign-in and two approvals.

approval.whenNeeded: To lift the history throttle, and for commercial distribution under Slack's terms.
approval.renewal: None, but listed apps are locked (decision 3).

stages.label: Gate
stages.detail: Active in the last 28 days, before you can submit.

stages.label: Step 1
stages.detail: Run in the console before submitting.

stages.label: Step 2
stages.detail: Preliminary review of listing and scopes. Resubmitting resets your place in the queue.

stages.label: Step 3
stages.detail: Functional review: a reviewer installs and tests. Queue place is kept.

rejections: Scopes for features that do not exist yet
approval.note: Slack will not speed up review for a launch date. Submit early.

ladder.limit: Other workspaces cannot install until distribution is active.

ladder.works: Any workspace can install, no review.
ladder.limit: History and thread reads: 1 request/min, 15 messages per call.
Standard rate-limit tiers. Changes need re-review.

notes.title: What this means for an agent
notes.text: Reading the last 200 messages of one busy channel takes about 14 minutes. Until you are listed, design around events (subscribe to new messages as they arrive) instead of polling history. Internal (customer-built) apps keep 50+ requests/min and 1,000 objects.

notes.title: Open conflict
notes.text: Slack's original May 29, 2025 post says existing installs of unlisted apps are not affected. Slack's changelog index says existing installs are affected from March 3, 2026. Plan as if all installs are throttled.

rows.breaks: Only uninstall or admin removal revokes it

rows.refresh: New one on every refresh; the old one is revoked
rows.breaks: Losing the newest refresh token kills the connection (`invalid_grant`)

tokens.note: PKCE is a separate opt-in on the OAuth & Permissions page, required only for custom URI scheme redirects. Whether rotation can be turned off after opting in was not checked.

rules.title: No LLM training
rules.text: on data from Slack APIs, for apps used outside the installing organization.

rules.title: No bulk export
rules.text: of messages and files without a separate agreement.

rules.title: Keep only what you need.
rules.text: Use, processing and retention must be the minimum the app needs to run.

rules.title: No persistent copies or indexes
rules.text: of other organizations' data via the Data Access and Real-time Search APIs. Brief caching only.

impact.title: Design impact
impact.text: "Sync the whole workspace into a vector database" is ruled out for a distributed app. Query live, cache briefly.

credentialHandoff.summary: Slack's manifest API can create apps and appears to return credentials to a backend tool, which could send them straight to a Composio auth config. Not yet verified. In our test the agent never opened the secret.

blockers.fix: Manage Distribution, then Activate Public Distribution

blockers.cause: URL differs from the registered one, or is not HTTPS
blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback from your Composio auth config

blockers.symptom: History calls return 15 messages and get rate limited
blockers.fix: Use events, or go through Marketplace review

blockers.cause: Rotation on, an old refresh token was reused
blockers.fix: Store the newest refresh token every time

blockers.cause: Scopes added but workspaces did not reinstall
blockers.fix: Ask users to reconnect; check granted scopes

blockers.symptom: Customer cannot install in their company workspace
